sentences.text:
Rep.By Its on 4 March, 2025
 The Honourable Sri Justice J.Sreenivas Rao
 Writ Petition No. 6394 Of 2015
Order:

This writ petition is filed seeking the following relief:
" ... to issue a Writ, order or direction more particularly one in the nature of WRIT OF MANDAMUS declaring the action of the respondents in not paying the compensation amount to the petitioners as per the claim petition dated 03.02.2015 and demolishing the petitioner's pan shop located at Garden & Restaurant situated at 9-1-40, S.D.
Road, Secunderabad vice proceedings No.C2/1618/2013 dated 28.03.2014 is illegal,
arbitrary and violation of Fundamental right guaranteed under the Constitution of India and violation of Article 19(1)(g), 21 and 300 A of the Constitution of India and consequently direct the respondents to grant compensation amount to then petitioners..."

2. Heard Mr. Nagula Srinivas Yadav, learned counsel for the petitioners, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for respondent Nos.1 to 3, and Mr. G.
Sundareshan, learned counsel representing Mr. K. S. Murthy, learned counsel for respondent No.4.
3. The grievance of the petitioners that their father, namely C. Yadagiri, entered into Tenancy agreement with Gulam Raza, who is the father of respondent No.4, and taken mulgi on rent by paying advance amount of Rs.5,000/- in the year 1958.
Respondent authorities acquired the premises of respndent No.4 for the purpose of construction of Metro Rail Project.

However, they have not paid any compensation to the petitioners, though the petitioners are entitled the compensation as per the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (Act No.30 of 2013) (hereinafter referred to,
as 'the Act').

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (Act No.30 of 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The petitioners have filed claim petition invoking the provisions of Section 9(3) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 claiming compensation before respondent No.3 and he has not passed any order.

He further submitted that as the respondents have not provided adequate compensation,
the petitioners filed representation on 03.02.2015.
However, respondent No.3 has not taken any steps to consider the same.
The action of respondent No.3 is contrary to law and violative of the provisions of the Act.

4. Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition submitted that if the claim petition submitted by the petitioners is still pending, respondent No.3 will consider the same in accordance with law.

5. Learned counsel for respondent No.4 submitted that respondent No.3 has to consider the objections submitted by the petitioners.

6. Having considered the rival submissions made by the respective parties, without expressing any view on the merits of the case, respondent No.3 is directed to consider the representation submitted by the petitioners dated 03.05.2015 and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law after giving notice and opportunity to the petitioners as well as respondent No.4, within a period of eight (8)
weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order, if not already disposed of.
It is made clear that the petitioners are entitled to raise all the grounds which are available under law.
7. With the above direction, the writ petition is disposed of.
No order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, pending if any, shall stand closed.
J. SREENIVAS RAO, J Date: 04.03.2025 mar C.Vijay Kumar S/O C.Yadagiri, vs The State Of Telangana, Rep.
